$description: The component contract: what each component is for, the options it takes, where it is implemented on each client, and where clients differ in a way its names do not show (`differences`: an option only some clients have, a part the platform draws, a different presentation for touch). Keep it in step with the components.

components.name: Button
components.purpose: An action. Use `primary` once per view, `secondary` for other actions, `ghost` for actions that stay out of the way, and `danger` for ones that destroy. With `selected` it is a toggle that stays pressed.
components.accessibility: The label is the accessible name. A loading button keeps its label and ignores presses. A button given `selected` reports whether it is pressed.

differences.note: A capsule instead of a rounded rectangle, at the touch control heights: `size.button-radius` and `size.control` take their touch values. The web clients switch to them on a touch screen too (`pointer: coarse`); Compose keeps the pointer values on the desktop.

components.name: TextField
components.purpose: A labelled text field with an optional description and error message. One line, or several with `multiline`.
components.accessibility: The label is always visible and tied to the input. An error replaces the description and is announced; clear it when the value changes.

components.name: Text
components.purpose: Text in one of the type roles.
components.accessibility: Pick the element or heading flag for the document outline, and the variant for the look.

components.name: Badge
components.purpose: A short status or category. The words carry the meaning; the color reinforces it.
components.accessibility: Never relies on color alone: it always has a text label.

components.name: CountBadge
components.purpose: A count on an icon, an avatar or a button: unread messages, items in a cart. A count of zero draws nothing.
components.accessibility: `label` says what is counted, such as "3 unread notifications". Without it assistive technology reads the number.

components.name: Banner
components.purpose: A message about the whole view or a section of it.
components.accessibility: Each tone has its own mark. `warning` and `danger` interrupt a screen reader; `info` and `success` wait their turn. The dismiss control has a name of its own.

components.name: Card
components.purpose: A surface that groups related content, with an optional picture, title, description and actions. With `onPress` the whole card is one button.
components.accessibility: The title is a heading. A pressable card is one button: put no other control inside it. A selected card is outlined, not only tinted.

components.name: Divider
components.purpose: A hairline between rows or sections.
components.accessibility: Decorative.

components.name: Spinner
components.purpose: Says that something is in progress and how long is unknown.
components.accessibility: Announced only when it has a label. With reduced motion on the web it pulses instead of spinning.

components.name: Switch
components.purpose: Turns a setting on or off, taking effect at once.
components.accessibility: Has the switch role. Without a visible label it needs an accessible label.

components.name: Checkbox
components.purpose: A choice that is applied later, with the form it belongs to.
components.accessibility: Without a visible label it needs an accessible label.

components.name: SegmentedControl
components.purpose: A choice between a few views or modes, all visible at once.
components.accessibility: A radio group: it needs a label that says what is being chosen. The selected segment is outlined as well as filled.

components.name: Avatar
components.purpose: Stands for a person or a team by a picture, or by their initials when there is none.
components.accessibility: Assistive technology gets the full name, with or without a picture.

components.name: AvatarStack
components.purpose: Several people in the room of one: overlapping avatars, and a count of those that did not fit.
components.accessibility: One image whose name is every person's name, or `label`. The avatars inside are hidden from assistive technology.

components.name: ProgressBar
components.purpose: How far along something is, from 0 to 1.
components.accessibility: The label says what is progressing; it is read with the percentage.

components.name: Icon
components.purpose: A drawing from design/icons, in the color of the text around it. `filled` marks a selected state on an icon made of closed shapes.
components.accessibility: Decoration unless it has a label, which names it for assistive technology. An arrow or a chevron can mirror in a right-to-left layout.

components.name: ListRow
components.purpose: One line of a list or a settings screen.
components.accessibility: With an action the whole row is a button, so do not put another control in `trailing`.

components.name: IconButton
components.purpose: A button that holds only an icon, in Button's variants, sizes and states. Use it where the icon is familiar and room is short.
components.accessibility: `label` is required: it is the accessible name, since there is no visible text. The pressable area is at least the minimum target even when the square is smaller.

differences.note: A circle instead of a rounded square, at the touch control heights: it takes Button's corner, `size.button-radius`, and `size.control` at their touch values. The web clients switch to them on a touch screen too (`pointer: coarse`); Compose keeps the pointer values on the desktop.

components.name: Chip
components.purpose: A choice that filters what is shown. Unlike a Badge it is pressed; a selected chip is tinted, outlined and marked with a check.
components.accessibility: A toggle button that reports whether it is selected.

components.name: ChipBar
components.purpose: A row of chips that scrolls sideways when it does not fit, and never wraps.
components.accessibility: A group named by `label`. It holds no state: the app decides which chips are selected.

components.name: Tabs
components.purpose: Switches between views inside one screen. For two to four short modes a SegmentedControl is lighter; Tabs is for more items, longer labels, or a row that may scroll.
components.accessibility: A tab list with a selected tab. The component is only the row: the app shows the matching view.

components.name: Menu
components.purpose: A list of actions that opens from a control: a popup where a pointer is used, a bottom sheet where fingers are.
components.accessibility: A menu with menu items. The trigger says that it opens a menu and whether it is open; Escape or Back closes it and focus returns to the trigger.

differences.note: Opens as a BottomSheet titled with `label`, its items full list rows, instead of a popup of compact rows lined up with the trigger, so `align` changes nothing. A tap outside, a drag down or Back closes it without choosing. Compose on the desktop opens the popup, as the pointer clients do.

components.name: Dialog
components.purpose: A window that interrupts the screen for a confirmation or a short task.
components.accessibility: A modal dialog named by its title. Focus moves into it, stays inside it, and returns on close. Escape, Back and the scrim close it unless `dismissible` is off.

components.name: Toast
components.purpose: A short message about what just happened, which leaves on its own. It can offer one action, such as Undo.
components.accessibility: Announced politely, without taking focus. Do not put the only way to an action in a toast.

components.name: Tooltip
components.purpose: Names a control when the pointer rests on it or the keyboard focuses it. Pointer clients only: there is no hover on a touch screen.
components.accessibility: Describes the control; it is not the control's name, which the control still needs.

components.name: Skeleton
components.purpose: Holds the place of content that is loading, in the shape of what will come.
components.accessibility: Hidden from assistive technology: the screen that shows skeletons says that it is loading.

components.name: SearchField
components.purpose: A text field for a query, with a search mark and a control that clears it.
components.accessibility: `label` is required and not shown: it names the field. The clear control has a name of its own.

components.name: RadioGroup
components.purpose: One choice among a few, applied later with the form it belongs to. For a choice that takes effect at once, a SegmentedControl is the usual pick.
components.accessibility: A radio group named by its visible legend. The whole row of an option is pressable, and the chosen one has a dot, not only a color.

components.name: Select
components.purpose: A field for choosing one option from a list too long to show at once. The list opens as a popup where a pointer is used and as a bottom sheet where fingers are.
components.accessibility: The field says that it opens a list and whether it is open. The list is a listbox, and the chosen option is marked with a check.

differences.note: Its options open as full list rows of a BottomSheet titled with `label`, instead of a popup as wide as the field. A tap outside, a drag down or Back closes it without choosing. Compose on the desktop opens the popup, as the pointer clients do.

components.name: DatePicker
components.purpose: A field for choosing one day. Closed, it looks like a Select. Pressed, it opens a calendar of one month: a popup where a pointer is used, a bottom sheet where fingers are. On React Native the calendar is the system's.
components.accessibility: The field is a button named by the chosen day and the label; it says that it opens a dialog and whether it is open, and the error describes it. The calendar is a grid of days, each named in full; the chosen day is selected and today is the current date. The arrow keys move a day or a week, Page Up and Page Down a month (with Shift a year), Home and End to the first and last day of the month, never past min or max. Enter or Space chooses and closes; Escape or Back closes without choosing. Focus returns to the field.

differences.note: The calendar opens in a BottomSheet titled with `label` instead of a popup under the field, its days at the touch value of `size.calendar-day` (48) unless seven of them are wider than the sheet. A tap outside, a drag down or Back closes it without choosing. Compose on the desktop opens the popup, as the pointer clients do. The web clients keep the popup on a touch screen, with the touch day size (`pointer: coarse`).

The calendar is the system's, shown through Expo UI: Material 3's date dialog on Android, where OK chooses the day and Cancel, Back or a tap outside closes it without choosing, and the iOS calendar in a BottomSheet titled with `label`, where a press on a day chooses it at once and Done, a drag down or a tap outside closes the sheet. It follows the device's language, region and calendar, so the names, the first day of the week, the keys and what a screen reader hears are the system's, and `previousLabel` and `nextLabel` are ignored. `color.date-picker` colors Android's dialog and tints the iOS calendar; their shapes, type and sizes are the system's, so `size.calendar-day` does not apply. The field is drawn from the tokens, like Select's.
Names the button under the iOS calendar that closes the sheet; `Done` unless it is given. Android's dialog has its own OK and Cancel, in the device's language.

components.name: DateRangePicker
components.purpose: A field for choosing a range of days, a start and an end, as for a stay or a trip. Closed, it looks like a DatePicker and shows both days. Pressed, it opens a calendar where the first day pressed starts the range and the second ends it: a popup of two months side by side where a pointer is used, a tall bottom sheet of months scrolling down where fingers are.
components.accessibility: The field is a button named by the chosen range and the label; it says that it opens a dialog and whether it is open, and the error describes it. The calendar is a grid of days for each month shown, named by its month and allowing more than one selected day; each day is named in full, the two ends after startLabel and endLabel, and every day of the range is selected. The keys are DatePicker's. Enter or Space on a day sets the start and moves to the next day, and the moves after it preview the range; Enter or Space again sets the end. A day before the start starts again from there. Days the length does not allow as the end cannot be chosen. Escape or Back closes and drops an unfinished range. Focus returns to the field.

differences.note: The popup shows one month instead of two where two do not fit beside each other (a window narrower than about 640 px).

components.name: Slider
components.purpose: Picks a number in a range by dragging, or with the arrow keys.
components.accessibility: A slider named by its label, with its value, minimum and maximum. Each key press moves it one step.

components.name: Thumbnail
components.purpose: A picture in a fixed shape, for a video, an article or a product, with an optional badge and a bar for how much was watched.
components.accessibility: `alt` describes the picture; an empty `alt` makes it decoration.

components.name: MediaCard
components.purpose: A thumbnail with its title and details: a video in a feed, an article in a list. Vertical, or horizontal with the picture at the start.
components.accessibility: A pressable card is one button named by its title and details. Its action is a control of its own.

components.name: SectionHeader
components.purpose: The title row of a group of content, with an optional description and an action such as "See all".
components.accessibility: The title is a heading, at the level given for the document outline.

components.name: Sidebar
components.purpose: The top-level places of an app where a pointer is used, the counterpart of TabBar on touch. Pointer clients only. Collapsed, it shows icons only.
components.accessibility: Navigation named by `label`. The current item says it is the current page; collapsed items keep their names and show them in tooltips.

components.name: EmptyState
components.purpose: What a screen says when it has nothing to show, and the one thing to do about it.
components.accessibility: The icon is decoration; the title says what is missing.

components.name: Accordion
components.purpose: Items whose bodies open and close under their titles. One at a time, or several with `multiple`.
components.accessibility: Each title row is a button that says whether its body is expanded.

components.name: TopBar
components.purpose: The bar at the top of a screen: a title, a back action and a trailing action.
components.accessibility: The title is a heading. The back button has a press area as large as the smallest touch target.

components.name: TabBar
components.purpose: Switches between the three to five top-level places of an app.
components.accessibility: A tab list. The selected tab sits in a pill, so the selection does not depend on color.

components.name: BottomSheet
components.purpose: A panel that slides up over the screen for a short task or a set of choices.
components.accessibility: Modal. Closes on a tap outside, a drag down, or the back button.
